D.treatment: observing another student’s complete failed problem-solving process
D.comparison: engaging in problem solving and failing oneself

cells.quote: In fact, students who observed the complete PF process even outperformed students who engaged in PF themselves.
cells.note: The study also reports that prior knowledge moderated this effect; the reported contrast was from an ANCOVA controlling for mathematical ability and prior knowledge.

O.outcome_detail: choice of interleaved versus blocked practice

cells.quote: Students’ learning strategy decisions, however, did not benefit from the metacognitive prompt.
cells.note: The study text reports no benefit from the prompt but does not state whether participants were randomly assigned to the prompt and control conditions.

cells.quote: The percentage of students who chose interleaved practice increased from 13 to 40%.
cells.note: The study reports a significant Cochran's Q test for strategy decisions increasing over time, χ2(2) = 43.531, p < 0.001; no effect size was printed.
